title: Marnie's Super Tidy Boat
markdown:
Sunshine bounced off Marnie the cat’s blue boat until the canal looked freshly polished. Saturday sat on the water like a clean plate. Ropes lay in tight coils. Knobs shone. The kettle waited in its exact cupboard, as if it already knew the rules.

Heddwyn the owl settled on the willow by the towpath. “Ready to dash?” he asked, blinking against the glitter.

Marnie flicked her tail. “My friends are coming. I want everything perfectly tidy.”

Jules the mouse zoomed aboard and skidded to a polite stop by the biscuit drawer. Captain Ash followed with a deck-stomping ahoy and a grin that made the brass fittings look extra proud of themselves.

“Welcome aboard,” Marnie said. “Just a moment.”

She fetched her paints. On the tea cupboard she lettered CUPBOARD: TEAS ONLY. On the drawer, DRAWER: BISCUITS & JAM. On the mooring rope, ROPE: MOORING USE ONLY. The boat became a little harbour of labels.

“Amazing signs,” Captain Ash said.

Jules twitched his whiskers. “Teas only? What about a biscuit?”

“Biscuits live in the biscuit drawer,” Marnie told him, as if the sentence itself were a coil of rope.

Captain Ash wanted tea and found it at once. Then he wanted a biscuit. He opened the drawer and dug, dug, dug, until the jam jar rolled and the biscuits turned up at the bottom. “Blast and barnacles,” he muttered, holding a crumbly prize as if it had been hiding on purpose.

Jules tugged the blanket box for a cushion. The blankets were stuffed so tight the lid came up with a flump and a sigh. “Oh dear,” he squeaked, peering into a nest of wool.

A gust shoved the boat. Water slapped the hull. “The mooring rope,” Captain Ash called. “We need it now.”

He darted to the sign, read ROPE: MOORING USE ONLY, and grabbed. The rope had been coiled so neatly it had become a knot with opinions. Jules pulled. Heddwyn hopped closer and hooted encouragement from the rail. They heaved together until the rope snapped free and the boat nudged safely back to the bank.

Captain Ash wiped his brow. “Your signs are precise, Marnie. A bit too precise for a jolly day.”

Marnie looked at Jules’s worried whiskers and Captain Ash’s flustered ears. The boat still gleamed. It did not feel glad.

She set her paintbrush down. “Perfect should be happy and easy too.”

They made a new system on the same Saturday sun. Tea still lived in its cupboard, with room for a biscuit if a biscuit wanted company. Blankets and cushions shared their box, warm against one another. The rope stayed tidy, but a loop hung where a paw could find it.

The canal winked. The knobs still sparkled. The signs looked a little less stern.

“Today,” Marnie said, tail flicking, “is going to be a good one.”

They slipped the easy rope, and the blue boat eased down the water, tidy enough to shine and loose enough to laugh.
characters: Marnie (super-tidy boat cat), Jules (zoomie canal mouse), Captain Ash (booming canal captain)
author: StoryGen Community
